While it is most prominently celebrated in Mexico, Día de los Muertos has gained recognition worldwide and is observed in various forms across Central America, South America, and even parts of the United States. Its cultural significance was recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2008.
